panels.title: Category boundary
ascii_lines: TRIBE -> no single universal sociological checklist
SCHEDULED TRIBE -> constitutional notification under Article 342
CONTINUUM -> historical thesis about long caste-society interaction
RULE -> the thesis never overrides the legal category
MUST REMEMBER: Tribal societies must be analysed through kinship, territory, livelihood,
political organisation, exchange, religion and state-market interfaces, with isolation,
assimilation, integration, dispossession, migration and self-governance treated as
historically variable processes.
source_references: What a tribe is and is not
The tribe-caste continuum and its limit

panels.title: Three policy positions
ascii_lines: ELWIN -> isolation, shield from market and settler exploitation
GHURYE -> assimilation, absorption as backward Hindus
NEHRU -> integration, development on tribals' own genius
OUTCOME -> none fully implemented, uneven acculturation followed

panels.title: Panchsheel content
ascii_lines: OWN GENIUS -> development on tribal terms
LAND AND FOREST -> rights retained rather than surrendered
SERVICES -> education, health and administration supplied
REJECTED -> both museum isolation and forced absorption

panels.title: Why displacement recurs
ascii_lines: RESOURCE GEOGRAPHY -> minerals, forests and hydel in tribal regions
PROJECT SITING -> mining, dams and industrial corridors
LOSS -> subsistence base and identity anchored in that land
EXPERIENCE -> development felt as trade-off, not shared gain
source_references: Why projects are sited in tribal regions

panels.title: Two mechanisms of land loss
ascii_lines: DISPLACEMENT -> acute, project-driven, single event
LAND ALIENATION -> slow transfer through debt or encroachment
REMEDY 1 -> resettlement design and livelihood restoration
REMEDY 2 -> restriction and restoration of transferred land

panels.title: Rehabilitation test
ascii_lines: LAND FOR LAND -> was an equivalent land base restored
LIVELIHOOD -> was the earning system rebuilt, not just paid for
COMMUNITY -> was the village relocated intact or scattered
VERDICT -> restoration means gain, compensation alone means loss
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Scheduled Tribe, tribe, indigenous people, Particularly Vulnerable Tribal
Group and forest dweller are not synonyms; Fifth Schedule, Sixth Schedule, PESA 1996 and
Forest Rights Act 2006 have distinct territorial, institutional and rights boundaries.

panels.title: Vulnerability card
ascii_lines: SOURCE -> Ministry of Tribal Affairs list dated 9 July 2024
COUNT -> 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
SPREAD -> 18 States and the UT of Andaman and Nicobar Islands
CRITERIA -> pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, subsistence economy
source_references: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups as the sharpest case

panels.title: Aggregation split
ascii_lines: AGGREGATE FOR -> notification, entitlement portability, atrocity protection
DISAGGREGATE FOR -> livelihood design and scheme targeting
VARIATION -> forest-dependent, settled cultivator, urban tribal worker
CONTEXT -> Fifth Schedule belts against Sixth Schedule polities
source_references: Aggregation for rights, disaggregation for design
Fifth Schedule, Sixth Schedule and identity assertion

panels.title: Knowledge domains
ascii_lines: ECOLOGICAL -> seasonal indicators, fire and fallow practice
MEDICINAL -> plant remedies held in practitioner lineages
GOVERNANCE -> customary rules on forest produce, grazing, water
CRAFT AND COSMOLOGY -> apprenticeship technique and sacred groves

panels.title: Mode contrast
ascii_lines: EMBEDDED -> held in practice, not abstracted into models
COLLECTIVE -> authored by a community, not an individual
ORAL AND PLACE-SPECIFIC -> transmitted by speech, indexed to one tract
VALIDATION -> long-run use rather than controlled testing

panels.title: Erosion and prohibition
ascii_lines: DISPLACEMENT -> severs the ecology the knowledge was indexed to
SCHOOLING AND MARKET -> break oral transmission chains
PROHIBITION 1 -> no substitute for public health or formal education
PROHIBITION 2 -> no unverified remedy attributed to a named tribe
source_references: Scale, PYQ routes and the answer spine

panels.title: Tribal answer spine
ascii_lines: OPEN -> state the opinion and the framing being tested
BODY -> displacement axis, then rehabilitation adequacy
ADD -> what the framing omits: identity, services, self-governance
CLOSE -> graded verdict with the dated official evidence
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Use central Indian, Northeast, Himalayan, island and pastoral examples,
including Bhil, Gond, Santhal, Naga and PVTG variation; avoid primitive-versus-modern
binaries, and distinguish notified status, statutory entitlement, implementation and lived
outcome.
source_references: Scale, PYQ routes and the answer spine
